transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Leah Park (SolarWind FinOps), Omar Khalid (Platform), Rita Chen (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be partial):
- Walked through Redwood Console per-route telemetry and bill-slice cost dashboard
- Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for low-latency inference and FinOps reporting needs
- Agreed to trial with 3 routes and share pricing + SOC2 docs

Topics covered: per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, sampling and aggregation windows, KV cache effects on cost, PII/data residency concerns, pilot plan, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright, hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, um I'm the AE on the account. we've got Carlos here, our solutions engineer, he'll run the demo, and um yeah, can you each say hi quickly? just to confirm names.
[00:15] Leah: Hey, Leah here. thanks for doing this. excited to see the billing side, we've got a lot of pressure from finance to understand per-feature chargebacks.
[00:22] Omar: Omar, platform engineering, hi.
[00:24] Rita: Rita, security. quick heads up, I'll mostly be listening for compliance stuff.
[00:28] Carlos: great, thanks — quick agenda, I'll show the console, then drill into per-route cost, show the bill-slice report and the tracing for inference requests, and then we'll stop for Q&A and next steps.
[00:38] Maya: perfect, yeah and Leah told me ahead of time that their big needs are: ability to tie costs back to specific product routes and customers, exportable billing for FinOps, and a pilot timeline in the next 2–3 weeks.
[00:48] Leah: correct, ideally we want to charge back to product lines and be able to see if new prompt templates cause cost spikes.
[00:55] Carlos: okay sharing my screen — bear with me, sometimes the console rendering is a little slow on my VPN. so this is the Redwood Console home, note the usage lenses card, you can slice by model, by route, and by token type.
[01:12] Carlos: jumping into routes — here are the routes that Maya provisioned for your trial org: billing-invoice, customer-support-chat, and insights-summarize. each route has throughput, p90 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:28] Leah: the p90 looks good, but can you show how tokens are counted? we have some internal re-tokenization for prompts.
[01:34] Carlos: yeah good q, tokens are counted at the ingress point, we do per-request token sizing but we also show 'charged tokens' after our batching and prefix-caching heuristics. so if you have a lot of identical prefaces, the prefix/KV cache will reduce charged tokens; the console shows both raw and billed token counts.
[01:53] Omar: does that caching affect latency for tail requests? we can't have cold cache spikes for our SLA.
[01:58] Carlos: right, cache warm-up is an operational thing — you can set 'cache policy' on the route: aggressive for internal batch jobs, conservative for low-latency user-facing routes. we also show latency breakdown per route so you can see the hit rate and the KV miss penalty.
[02:15] Maya: quick aside — for dedicated deployments you'd be able to reserve capacity which flattens latency, but it's a commit and pricing tradeoff.
[02:24] Leah: about that — finance asked whether dedicated is worth it for our chat product, it's high volume but also cost-sensitive. what's the usual recommendation?
[02:33] Carlos: runs on a few axes: predictable throughput (if you need consistent p95 under 200ms) go dedicated; if you want to minimize committed spend and burst, hosted plus autoscaling and route-level throttles is cheaper. Also quantization and batching settings impact unit cost dramatically.
[02:47] Rita: security question — if we go hosted, what data leaves our VPC? we need to keep PII in our control.
[02:54] Maya: good question. Redwood Hosted processes inference in our managed infra but we support private deployment and VPC peering for customers that need it. we also integrate with customer KMS for key handling — note the docs have the KMS and HSM sections, I'll share them.
[03:10] Carlos: back to the console — here's the bill-slice view, it's our per-route billed cost breakdown over the chosen window. you can pivot by day, week, or billing cycle. notice the 'cost delta' column which highlights routes with sudden token inflation.
[03:26] Carlos: I'm going to filter to the last 30 days and group by product tag; you can tag routes with your internal product codes and then export to CSV for FinOps ingestion.
[03:38] Leah: can we map cost back to end-customers? like show route X cost for customer Y?
[03:43] Carlos: yes if you pass customer_id at request time as metadata, the console's billing export will include it. we also offer a sample BigQuery export sink for large customers.
[03:54] Omar: what's the format of the export? we prefer parquet.
[03:58] Carlos: currently we do newline JSON and BigQuery ingest, but parity parquet exports are on the roadmap — I noted parity with our product team last week.
[04:08] Leah: another thing — we have a few short-running bulk jobs that produce lots of tokens, how do you separate those?
[04:14] Carlos: we support route tags and request-level metadata; you can create a separate route for batch jobs or tag them and then exclude from product billing views. the console lets you create custom 'billing lenses' with include/exclude rules.
[04:26] Maya: transcription note — sometimes the automatic labs will mislabel system names, but you can see the raw logs in the route inspector.
[04:34] Carlos: now drilling into an example — route 'insights-summarize' spike on Sep 14. click to expand... here's per-request trace, token breakdown, and the suggested action from the Optimize tool: reduce temperature and enable 4-bit quantization for that model family.
[04:56] Leah: hmm reducing temperature for summaries might change quality — can we run A/B and track eval metrics?
[05:02] Carlos: yes we have built-in evaluation sets you can attach to routes; console will show quality regression alerts tied to a prompt set. we can also compare BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim similarity if you feed reference data.
[05:16] Rita: how does the eval data get stored? we have retention and PII constraints.
[05:21] Maya: evals are optional and can be configured to redact or hash PII; we can also keep eval data in your VPC for private deployments.
[05:31] Carlos: jumping to the cost model tab — here's a per-token cost model with breakdown for GPU hours, provisioning, and amortized infra. for hosted customers we show effective unit price after cache and batching savings.
[05:47] Carlos: one thing to point out — the console's cost projection tool can run simulations: if you change batching from 1 to 8, or enable prefix caching for 20% of traffic, you'll see projected monthly cost impact.
[06:01] Leah: can you show a 'what-if' where we enable batching=4 for support-chat?
[06:06] Carlos: sure — toggling to batching=4 gives estimated 34% cost savings on that route but increases median latency by roughly 40ms. it's a typical tradeoff: optimize for cost or latency per route.
[06:21] Omar: do you allow mixed policies per endpoint? like some requests flagged low-latency bypass batching?
[06:27] Carlos: yes you can annotate requests with a priority header; high-priority bypasses batching and gets routed to low-latency pool, the others go through batch queue.
[06:35] Leah: how visible is that split in the billing? will we get a combined number or route-level split?
[06:40] Carlos: you get both — the route shows aggregated cost and you can break down by priority tag. that shows up in the 'telemetry slices' export.
[06:48] Maya: quick demo pause — any clarifying q's before I keep going?
[06:53] Leah: yes, what's the SLA for hosted? also do you have SOC 2 and ISO?
[06:58] Maya: hosted SLA depends on tier; standard is 99.9% with availability and latency targets; enterprise tiers with dedicated commits can get 99.95+ and priority support. we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; I will share the cert pack after the call.
[07:14] Rita: network diagrams and our legal team will want data flow details.
[07:18] Maya: noted — I'll include the network diagrams and a short explanation of where data is stored and how KMS integration works.
[07:25] Carlos: resuming console, here's anomaly detection — alerts tie back to routes and you can set thresholds on token growth and p95 latency; alerts can open a ticket in Jira or trigger a webhook.
[07:38] Omar: curious about telemetry costs — does more telemetry add to our bill? we have to watch costs of observability.
[07:45] Carlos: basic telemetry is included, but high-granularity traces and long retention has a small cost; we provide retention tiers and a rollup mode which stores aggregated metrics to reduce storage cost.
[07:58] Leah: okay, show me the export again — I want to see the columns we get.
[08:02] Carlos: exporting now, here's a snippet: timestamp, route_id, request_id, model_family, raw_tokens, billed_tokens, cost_usd, customer_id, priority, tag. note that PII fields only appear if you pass them; we recommend hashing customer identifiers.
[08:21] Leah: good, that should plug into our FinOps pipeline. for the pilot, we want sample data for 30 days so finance can validate models. is that doable?
[08:29] Maya: yes, we can seed a sample billing export for the pilot with synthetic traffic mirroring your patterns. I'll prepare that.
[08:36] Carlos: now quick look at the 'routes map' view — this is useful for platform teams to see dependencies, model variants, and fallback policies. you can see that billing-invoice route falls back from the 40B model to a 7B distill when latency goes high.
[08:53] Omar: how do you measure fallback frequency? we need a gauge for how often we get degraded outputs.
[08:58] Carlos: we surface fallback rate per route and per model variant. plus we link to the 'quality regression' monitor if fallbacks cause output changes.
[09:08] Leah: we also care about multi-region routing for customers in EU. can we show EU-only data residency?
[09:15] Maya: yes, you can restrict routes to a region or set policy to run EU data in EU-only hosts. for private/on-prem we obviously keep everything in your network.
[09:24] Rita: default logs retention? our legal requires 90 days.
[09:28] Maya: default is 30, enterprise can extend to 90+ and we can put logs in your S3 bucket on request.
[09:35] Carlos: jumping ahead — Optimize suggestions: here's a route-level recommendation list, sorted by expected $ savings; example: enable dynamic quantization for 'billing-invoice' -> est. $9k/mo savings.
[09:49] Leah: how confident are the savings estimates? do you validate them?
[09:53] Carlos: estimates come from past telemetry and actual execution profiles; we show confidence bands and also allow you to run an on-prem benchmark. for high-precision we recommend a short controlled run.
[10:05] Maya: quick check — any concerns about model parity when using quantized variants?
[10:10] Omar: yes we saw hallucination increases when we tried a low-precision variant last year.
[10:15] Carlos: understood; that's why our rollouts include A/B evaluation hooks and automatic rollback if eval metrics cross thresholds. you can set tolerances per route.
[10:25] Leah: can we bring our own models? we have some proprietary family models.
[10:29] Carlos: BYO models are supported via the Private deployment; we can also host your model if you provide a container image and weights under an enterprise agreement.
[10:38] Rita: what about keys for BYO? we need HSM-level control.
[10:42] Maya: we support KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys in some tiers.
[10:50] Carlos: I'm going to demo the 'route investigator' — it shows request timelines and the token waterfall. notice here, a single long prefix accounts for 60% of billed tokens, so the recommendation is to move that prefix into a cached system prompt or reduce repetition.
[11:11] Leah: aha that's the thing we suspected, templates are inefficient. can the console automatically rewrite prompts?
[11:16] Carlos: we have a 'prompt suggestions' lab that flags repeated context and suggests compressed templates, but it doesn't rewrite without approval. it gives you a proposed prompt with estimated token delta.
[11:27] Omar: in terms of rollout, what's a minimal pilot we can do that gives finance confidence?
[11:32] Maya: three routes, one for chat, one for summaries, one for billing-invoice (batch). run for 2 weeks with synthetic and real traffic combined, we'll provide the billing export and a cost model comparison.
[11:45] Leah: that sounds fine. what about success metrics? Leah: success for us is being able to attribute >95% of monthly cost to product routes and demonstrate a >20% reduction in unit cost for one of the routes after tuning.
[11:57] Carlos: noted — we'll build the pilot dashboard with those metrics.
[12:02] Carlos: another subtlety — tokenization differences across client SDKs. be careful if you preprocess in Go vs Python. the console normalizes raw tokens but we include a reconciliation guide.
[12:16] Omar: good to know.
[12:20] Maya: quick pause, any security red flags yet? Rita?
[12:23] Rita: mostly standard questions, I'd like the SOC docs and network flow, and I'd like to run a short pen-test scope when pilot hits 2 weeks in.
[12:31] Maya: sure, we'll coordinate with your security team.
[12:35] Carlos: moving to the demo final piece — the 'cost anomaly playbook' feature. you can define runbooks that map alerts to actions: throttle traffic, switch to cheaper model, notify Slack channel, or open a support ticket.
[12:50] Leah: can playbooks be templated across routes? we have dozens of small product routes.
[12:55] Carlos: yes, you create a playbook template and apply it to multiple routes; templates support variables.
[13:03] Leah: you mentioned big query earlier — do we need to keep both BigQuery and the console?
[13:08] Carlos: console is the UI for ops and quick exports; BigQuery export is for long-term analytics and integration with your FinOps stack. many customers use both.
[13:18] Omar: what's the retention for BigQuery exports? that's our own setting.
[13:22] Carlos: correct, you control retention once the export lands in your project.
[13:27] Maya: okay, jumping to Q&A from the chat — Leah asks about cost granularity to user sessions — you could attach session id as a metadata tag and then run session-level cost reports but that is higher cardinality and impacts export size.
[13:44] Leah: is there sampling for high-cardinality tags?
[13:47] Carlos: yes you can sample tagging for telemetry while still getting aggregated totals for billing.
[13:52] Rita: another compliance point — can we restrict who inside our org can see billing exports? we need strict RBAC.
[13:59] Maya: RBAC is supported; console roles can be limited to route-level visibility and exports restricted to finance group.
[14:07] Carlos: demo note — here's the playbook where alert on token inflation triggers a canary rollback to the cached model variant.
[14:20] Leah: cool. any latency numbers when we rollback?
[14:24] Carlos: rollback is near-instant for model variant selection, the bigger impact is cold cache for the new variant; the console shows expected transient latency curves.
[14:35] Omar: operational question — for dedicated pools, do you let us pick GPU family?
[14:40] Carlos: yes, dedicated capacity configs let you choose GPU family and model families; we also offer recommended defaults based on your workload.
[14:48] Leah: pricing — we've seen pricing variability across vendors; can we get a sample cost comparison with Anthropic?
[14:55] Maya: we can prepare a competitor cost sheet, though pricing comparisons are always workload dependent. I'll include a side-by-side for the pilot routes.
[15:04] Leah: please include assumptions for throughput, batch size, and average sequence length.
[15:09] Maya: will do.
[15:11] Carlos: jumping to the end-to-end export demo — I'm kicking off a sample billing export now; it will include route tags, billed tokens, and a cost allocation column.
[15:22] Carlos: while that's running, quick question — do you have any internal enforcement for model quality thresholds? like a max allowed semantic drift?
[15:29] Leah: not formalized, we use ad-hoc QA. part of this pilot is to create that gating.
[15:35] Carlos: perfect — the console's eval hooks will help you formalize that.
[15:41] Maya: we've got about 10 minutes left, want to cover pilot logistics and next steps?
[15:46] Leah: yes please.
[15:48] Maya: proposed pilot scope: 3 routes, 2-week run, synthetic + real traffic, cost export for 30 days, quality evaluation set for 1 route, security review after week 1. deliverables: billing export, pilot dashboard, cost model, rollouts plan.
[16:03] Leah: timeline? we need to start by Oct 18 to align with finance cycle.
[16:08] Maya: we can start Oct 18 — Carlos will provision the trial org and enable telemetry by Oct 12 so you have a week to sanity-check configs.
[16:17] Omar: do you need anything from our infra team to get telemetry running?
[16:21] Carlos: just an API key and optional BigQuery sink credentials (or an S3 bucket) and the route names. we also have a quickstart script to instrument the SDK.
[16:31] Leah: budget approval is pending but likely, we should be fine.
[16:36] Rita: for security review, I'll send a list of questions; please expect a short call to go through the network diagram.
[16:42] Maya: sounds good. last section — I'll recap next steps then open floor.
[16:46] Maya: recap: 1) Maya send pricing and competitor comparison + sample billing export (due 2027-10-05). 2) Carlos set up trial org and enable per-route telemetry for the three routes (due 2027-10-12). 3) Rita and Maya schedule security scoping call (date tbd). 4) Pilot kickoff target week of 2027-10-18.
[17:06] Leah: that's perfect.
[17:08] Omar: one last nit — can we anonymize user ids in the export for compliance?
[17:12] Carlos: yes we can hash or redact customer_id field; we'll apply your preference.
[17:17] Leah: thanks everyone.
[17:19] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up in email and I'll attach SOC docs and the pricing sheet.
[17:24] Rita: bye.
[17:26] Carlos: thanks, bye.

(End of recording)
